description:
Migrate the PLE scalar base and the two panel lane widths to resolved-once reads threaded through the recursion.

## Background

The proof-surface seam design (dev/active/7d7c647c/design.md) governs this task; read it in full. Its §3 fixes the three-part seam with probe-verified surface claims, §4 gives each field its name, kind, range, default-naming constant, mechanism and route-observation obligation, §5 records the decisions (D1 direct removal, D2 lane split, D3 opaque pin, D4 default naming, D5 public reporters, D6 source-level convention amendments), §6 enumerates the post-processing deletions, and §8 scopes the tasks. The follow-on migration design (dev/active/7d824b2f/design.md) supplies the shared field-kind, mechanism and test conventions.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: ple_in_place resolves ple.scalar_base_max_cols and the lane width for F::simd_ple_panel_lane() once and threads both through ple_in_place_window and ple_in_place_window_no_panel by parameter; the debug assertion relating panel width to scalar base moves to the resolve point over resolved values.
- [hard] REQ-02: ple_base_route and ple_panel_route(lane, win) are public and called by the dispatchers; per-lane installed-profile route files pass; the width assertions at the old sites are rewritten as route observations.
- [hard] REQ-03: The module walkthrough prose is updated; behaviour with no profile installed is unchanged.
